sources.details: Finite cards: 3 of 4 equally likely outcomes are cat, so P(cat)=3/4 and P(dog)=1/4; disjoint exhaustive events sum to 1. For independent answers, P(both)=.5*.5=.25. Natural log is inverse exp and log(ab)=log(a)+log(b) for a,b>0; -ln(.9)=.1053605, -ln(.5)=.6931472, -ln(.1)=2.3025851, -ln(.25)=1.3862944; derivative of -ln(p) is -1/p<0 for p>0, and limit as p goes to zero from above is positive infinity. Scores: row sums210,270 divided by3 give70,90; column sums140,160,180 divided by2 give70,80,90. Replacing80 by110 makes row240/3=80 and last column210/2=105. 2*3=6, reshaping to8 cells cannot preserve element count. Matrix product C_ij=sum_k A_ik B_kj: [2,1,0] produces[40,1], [1,2,1] produces[80,6]; bias[5,0] adds5 only to each cost; bias[8,0] yields[48,1],[88,6]. For L(w)=(w-3)^2, [L(w+h)-L(w)]/h=2(w-3)+h, so as h tends to0, L'=2(w-3); at1 it is-4, at1.4 it is-3.2. L(1)=4,L(1.1)=3.61 and decrease=.39. Updating w'=1-lr*(-4)=1+4lr gives1.4,3.4,5.4 for lr .1,.6,1.1, whose losses are2.56,.16,5.76. Since L>=0 with equality only at3, the minimum is w=3. The scalar derivative is the one-parameter gradient; with several differentiable coordinates the vector consists of partial derivatives, each holding the others fixed. The gradient only supplies local first-order information. Figure6 uses x=75+123w,y=430-34L: (1,4)->(198,294); (1.4,2.56)->(247.2,342.96); (3,0)->(444,430).
